title: Reasonable > Rational
coreMove: Prefer the plan you can keep through fear over the plan that wins only on paper.
sourcePressure: A money strategy must fit temperament, sleep, attention, and panic limits or its theoretical efficiency will not matter.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening Reasonable > Rational with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing Reasonable > Rational to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the reasonable move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of reasonable and rational

exampleSpecs.domain: a school pension committee choosing a simpler fund lineup employees will actually use
exampleSpecs.audience: a benefits chair balancing elegance and participation
exampleSpecs.stakes: the optimal menu fails if teachers freeze at enrollment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she removes three marginally superior options after watching staff abandon the form
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an enrollment form with too many tiny fund boxes

exampleSpecs.domain: a surgeon choosing a mortgage payment that lets him sleep after night calls
exampleSpecs.audience: a high earner rejecting the maximum approval number
exampleSpecs.stakes: the rational loan limit ignores fatigue, family stress, and error risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes post-call sleep hours beside the lender's approval before choosing the smaller house
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a mortgage preapproval letter beside a hospital call schedule

exampleSpecs.domain: a retiree keeping extra cash despite an advisor's efficient allocation model
exampleSpecs.audience: a retiree who values sleeping through downturns
exampleSpecs.stakes: selling during panic would cost more than the cash drag
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the advisor to price the cash against the bad decision it prevents during a 25 percent drawdown
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a portfolio printout with a handwritten sleep note in the margin

exampleSpecs.domain: a food truck owner selecting fixed-rate debt over cheaper variable debt
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner who knows anxiety changes daily decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: rate surprises could make him cut quality or hours
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he compares the cheaper loan to the menu changes he would make if rates jumped
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated menu beside two loan term sheets

exampleSpecs.domain: a language learner using a five-minute practice rule instead of an ideal one-hour plan
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner with inconsistent evenings
exampleSpecs.stakes: the perfect plan dies when life gets crowded
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares the abandoned hour-long schedule with the streak kept by one tiny daily recording
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a voice memo list with dates in a new language app

exampleSpecs.domain: a charitable foundation setting a spending rule board members can defend during recessions
